deck.title: General Characteristic Chemical Properties of the First Set of Transition Elements, Titanium to Copper

front_blocks.md: Define **complex**.

back_blocks.md: A **complex** is a molecule or ion formed by a central metal atom or ion surrounded by one or more ligands that donate lone pairs to form dative covalent bonds.

front_blocks.md: What shape and coordination number does [Cu(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>2+</sup> have?

back_blocks.md: [Cu(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>2+</sup> is **octahedral** with a coordination number of **6**. Six water ligands each donate a lone pair to form six dative covalent bonds with the central Cu<sup>2+</sup> ion.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Chloride ion ligands form octahedral complexes with Cu<sup>2+</sup> ions.

back_blocks.md: **False.** Chloride ions are large ligands, so only four fit around the central metal ion, forming a **tetrahedral** complex [CuCl<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2-</sup> with a coordination number of 4.

front_blocks.md: What is the overall charge of [Co(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>2+</sup> and how is it determined?

back_blocks.md: The overall charge is **2+**. It is calculated as the charge on Co<sup>2+</sup> (+2) plus the charge from six neutral water ligands (6 × 0), giving a total of +2.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The coordination number of a complex is equal to the number of ligands present.

back_blocks.md: **False.** The coordination number is the **number of dative covalent bonds** formed, not the number of ligands. A bidentate ligand contributes 2 to the coordination number despite being one ligand.

front_blocks.md: Define **ligand**.

back_blocks.md: A **ligand** is a molecule or ion that has one or more lone pairs of electrons, which it donates to a central metal atom or ion to form dative covalent bonds.

front_blocks.md: What is a monodentate ligand? Give two examples.

back_blocks.md: A **monodentate** ligand forms only **one** dative bond to the central metal ion. Examples include water (H<sub>2</sub>O) and ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>).

front_blocks.md: Why do larger monodentate ligands tend to form tetrahedral rather than octahedral complexes?

back_blocks.md: Larger ligands, such as Cl<sup>-</sup>, cause more steric repulsion. Only **four** of them can fit around the central metal ion, resulting in a **tetrahedral** geometry rather than six ligands in an octahedral arrangement.

front_blocks.md: Define **coordinate bond**.

back_blocks.md: A **coordinate bond** (also called a dative covalent bond) is a bond formed when one species donates both electrons in the shared pair, as occurs when a ligand bonds to a central metal ion in a complex.

front_blocks.md: Define **standard electrode potential**.

back_blocks.md: A **standard electrode potential** (*E*<sup>θ</sup>) is the potential of a half-cell measured relative to the standard hydrogen electrode under standard conditions, indicating how readily a species is reduced.

cards.front_md: Define **standard electrode potential**.
cards.back_md: A **standard electrode potential** (*E*<sup>θ</sup>) is the potential of a half-cell measured relative to the standard hydrogen electrode under standard conditions, indicating how readily a species is reduced.

front_blocks.md: How do you calculate the standard cell potential for a redox reaction?

back_blocks.md: *E*<sup>θ</sup><sub>cell</sub> = *E*<sup>θ</sup><sub>reduction</sub> − *E*<sup>θ</sup><sub>oxidation</sub>. A **positive** value indicates the reaction is feasible.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A more positive standard electrode potential means a species is more readily oxidised.

back_blocks.md: **False.** A more positive *E*<sup>θ</sup> means the species is more readily **reduced** (gains electrons more readily). The more negative the *E*<sup>θ</sup>, the more readily the species is oxidised.

front_blocks.md: Given *E*<sup>θ</sup> for Fe<sup>3+</sup>/Fe<sup>2+</sup> = +0.77 V and Cu<sup>2+</sup>/Cu<sup>+</sup> = +0.15 V, calculate *E*<sup>θ</sup><sub>cell</sub> for the reaction Fe<sup>3+</sup> + Cu<sup>+</sup> → Fe<sup>2+</sup> + Cu<sup>2+</sup>.

back_blocks.md: *E*<sup>θ</sup><sub>cell</sub> = (+0.77) − (+0.15) = **+0.62 V**. The positive value confirms the reaction is **feasible**.

front_blocks.md: Define **feasibility of a redox reaction**.

back_blocks.md: The half equation with the **less positive** (or more negative) standard electrode potential is reversed, so the species is **oxidised** rather than reduced.

front_blocks.md: Define **autocatalyst**.

back_blocks.md: An **autocatalyst** is a product of a reaction that catalyses the same reaction, causing it to accelerate as more product is formed. In the MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup>/C<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup> reaction, Mn<sup>2+</sup> acts as the autocatalyst.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In the reaction of Fe<sup>2+</sup> with MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> in acid, the endpoint is when a permanent pink colour appears.

back_blocks.md: **True.** The purple MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> colour disappears as it reacts with Fe<sup>2+</sup>. The endpoint is when all Fe<sup>2+</sup> has reacted and a trace of permanent **pink** appears, indicating a slight excess of MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup>.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In the Cu<sup>2+</sup>/I<sup>-</sup> titration, starch is added at the start to indicate the endpoint.

back_blocks.md: **False.** Starch is added when **most of the iodine colour has faded**, not at the start. It turns deep blue/black in the presence of the remaining I<sub>2</sub> and the endpoint is when this colour disappears.

front_blocks.md: In the Cu<sup>2+</sup>/I<sup>-</sup> system, what is the role of sodium thiosulfate in the second reaction?

back_blocks.md: **Sodium thiosulfate** reacts with the iodine produced: I<sub>2</sub> (aq) + 2S<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub><sup>2-</sup> (aq) → 2I<sup>-</sup> (aq) + S<sub>4</sub>O<sub>6</sub><sup>2-</sup> (aq). The moles of thiosulfate are used to calculate the **moles of Cu**<sup>**2+**</sup>.

front_blocks.md: In the MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup>/C<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup> reaction, the oxidation number of manganese changes from **..........**  to **..........** , so MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> is **..........** .

back_blocks.md: In the MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup>/C<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup> reaction, the oxidation number of manganese changes from **+7** to **+2**, so MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> is **reduced**.

front_blocks.md: Define **redox titration**.

back_blocks.md: A **redox titration** is a titration in which one species is oxidised and another is reduced, used to find the concentration of an unknown species by measuring the volume of a standard solution required to reach the endpoint.
